result: TNFR1, but not TNFR2, deficiency suppresses the Sharpin-deficient phenotype more efficiently than IL-1R1 loss. Tnfr1 deletion completely prevented dermatitis even after 35 weeks and partially ameliorated liver and splenic pathology, while Tnfr2 and Il1r1 deletion did not prevent multi-organ pathology.
evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C45, C48, C49, and C50 are well-supported by experimental data in Figure 1 showing that Shpnm/mTnfr1−/− mice had no disease at 35 weeks while Shpnm/mTnfr2−/− and Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice developed disease. The head-to-head comparison provides strong evidence for the differential roles of these receptors.

result: IL-1R1 deletion significantly delayed but did not prevent dermatitis in Sharpin-deficient mice. Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice had reduced epidermal hyperplasia at 13 weeks but developed disease by 19-20 weeks. Tnfr1 deletion was more effective at reducing leukocyte numbers than Il1r1 deletion.
evaluation: Claims C46, C47, and C101 are supported by data in Figures 1 and 10 showing delayed but not prevented dermatitis in Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice and differential effects on leukocyte numbers. This demonstrates IL-1R1 contributes to but is not the primary driver of disease.

result: Early inflammatory changes in cpdm skin include elevated TNF, IL-5, MCP-1, IL-12 p40, and increased F4/80+ macrophage infiltration in the dermis at 3 weeks before significant epidermal hyperplasia.
evaluation: Claims C51-C56 are supported by BioPlex cytokine analysis and immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2A-B showing elevated inflammatory mediators and macrophage infiltration at early time points. This provides evidence for the inflammatory milieu preceding overt disease.

result: Apoptosis is an early event in cpdm dermatitis, with cleaved caspase-3-positive cells present in the epidermis at 3 weeks before significant hyperplasia. Cleaved caspase-3-positive cells were also detected in liver and spleen but were much less frequent than in epidermis.
evaluation: Claims C57-C60 are supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2C showing cleaved caspase-3-positive cells at 3 weeks in epidermis and to a lesser extent in liver and spleen. This temporal relationship supports apoptosis as an early pathogenic event.

result: The hematopoietic system in isolation cannot cause Shpnm/m dermatitis. Wild-type mice reconstituted with Shpnm/m bone marrow did not develop any skin, liver, or spleen phenotype during 12 months of observation, demonstrating the inflammatory skin phenotype results from an intrinsic skin defect.
evaluation: Claims C61, C62, and C111 are strongly supported by bone marrow reconstitution experiments in Figure 3 showing no disease transfer over 12 months with high reconstitution efficiency. This extends prior 2-month studies and definitively establishes a skin-intrinsic defect.

result: TNF induces cell death with caspase-3 and -8 cleavage in Shpnm/m keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts. In keratinocytes, death was partially blocked by Q-VD-OPh or Nec-1. In dermal fibroblasts, death was almost completely blocked by Nec-1 but not Q-VD-OPh, and Nec-1 reduced caspase-8 and -3 cleavage.
evaluation: Claims C64-C70 are supported by in vitro cell death assays and western blots in Figure 4A-D showing TNF-induced caspase cleavage and differential sensitivity to inhibitors. The unexpected finding that Nec-1 blocks caspase activation in fibroblasts is particularly notable and well-documented.

result: Shpnm/m neutrophils, monocytes, and bone-marrow-derived macrophages were all sensitive to TNF-induced cell death, whereas wild-type cells were not. Neutrophil and monocyte death was more efficiently blocked by combined Nec-1 and Q-VD, while in macrophages Nec-1 alone was sufficient.
evaluation: Claims C71-C74 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4E showing TNF sensitivity of myeloid cells and differential responses to inhibitors. This suggests myeloid cell death may contribute to inflammation, though the speculation in C74 requires further validation.

result: LUBAC and its linear-ubiquitin-chain-forming activity are required for preventing TNF-induced keratinocyte death. Substantially reduced linear ubiquitylation was detected in TNFR1 signaling complexes from Shpnm/m MEFs, and HaCaT keratinocytes expressing catalytically inactive HOIPC885S were sensitive to TNF-induced death.
evaluation: Claims C75-C77 are supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 5A showing reduced linear ubiquitin in Shpnm/m cells and cell death assays in Figure 5B showing sensitivity of cells expressing catalytically inactive HOIP. This establishes the requirement for LUBAC catalytic activity.

result: Casp8 heterozygosity significantly delayed dermatitis in Sharpin-deficient mice. 12-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice had almost no epidermal hyperplasia, though one mouse developed hyperplasia by 15 weeks. However, Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice retained splenomegaly, liver inflammation, and lack of Peyer's patches.
evaluation: Claims C6, C78, C79, and C80 are supported by histological analysis and epidermal thickness measurements in Figure 6A-C showing marked delay in dermatitis but persistence of systemic phenotypes. This demonstrates tissue-specific roles for caspase-8 in the disease.

result: Bid deletion provided no protection from any aspect of the cpdm phenotype, indicating that caspase-8, but not BID, is an important driver of disease and that the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway is unlikely to play a significant role.
evaluation: Claims C81, C82, and C118 are supported by data in Figure 6A-D showing no protection in Shpnm/mBid−/− mice. This definitively rules out the type II apoptosis pathway and the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway as major contributors to disease.

result: Ripk3 deletion slightly delayed dermatitis in roughly half of 12-week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice, though all eventually developed severe disease before 18 weeks. However, 12-week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice had no liver inflammation and significantly less splenomegaly, suggesting RIPK3 contributes to the epidermal phenotype in a non-MLKL-dependent manner.
evaluation: Claims C83-C86 and C90 are supported by histological analysis in Figure 7A-D showing variable delay in dermatitis but consistent protection of liver and spleen. The inference that RIPK3 acts in a necroptosis-independent manner in skin is supported by comparison with Mlkl deletion data.

result: Mlkl deletion did not affect the Shpnm/m skin phenotype but significantly reduced splenomegaly and liver inflammation. 12-week-old Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice had similar epidermal phenotype to Shpnm/m mice but only 1 of 12 showed liver inflammation. This indicates RIPK3 and MLKL are important drivers of liver and splenic pathology.
evaluation: Claims C87-C89 and C112 are supported by data in Figure 7B-D showing differential effects on skin versus systemic organs. This demonstrates tissue-specific cell death mechanisms and establishes necroptosis as a driver of systemic but not skin pathology.

result: The skin and systemic phenotypes in Shpnm/m mice are separable. Sharpin deficiency triggers apoptosis in some tissues (skin) but necroptosis in others (liver, spleen, hematopoietic system), as demonstrated by differential effects of Mlkl and Casp8 deletion.
evaluation: Claims C114 and C125 are supported by the combined data from Figures 6-7 showing that Casp8 heterozygosity ameliorates skin but not systemic phenotypes while Mlkl deletion ameliorates systemic but not skin phenotypes. This is a key mechanistic insight.

result: Sharpin, Ripk3 and Casp8 triple deficiency caused perinatal lethality. Most Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice died between E17 and 1-2 days after birth at one facility, with no animals obtained at weaning. Two viable mice were obtained at a separate facility but appeared runted by 3 months and had disrupted splenic architecture.
evaluation: Claims C9, C91-C96, and C133 are supported by breeding data and histological analysis in Figure 8A-D showing significant perinatal lethality with variable penetrance. This unexpected finding is well-documented though the mechanism remains unclear. The variable penetrance across facilities is acknowledged.

result: Combined Ripk3 deletion and Casp8 heterozygosity almost completely suppressed the Sharpin-deficient phenotype, even restoring Peyer's patches. Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no skin, liver, or spleen pathology at 12 weeks and Peyer's patches were present. Most aged mice (45-67 weeks) had no skin phenotype, though one mouse developed dermatitis at 42 weeks.
evaluation: Claims C8, C97-C100, and C137 are strongly supported by comprehensive histological analysis in Figure 9A-E showing near-complete suppression of all disease manifestations including restoration of Peyer's patches. The single mouse developing late dermatitis suggests the single Casp8 allele can eventually drive disease.

result: The hematopoietic phenotype in Shpnm/m mice is driven predominantly by necroptosis. Caspase-8 heterozygosity or Bid deletion did not prevent leukocytosis, whereas Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion markedly reduced it. Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no white blood cell elevation.
evaluation: Claims C102-C106 are supported by ADVIA blood analysis in Figure 10 showing differential effects of genetic deletions on leukocyte numbers. The inference that necroptosis drives the hematopoietic phenotype is well-supported by the Mlkl deletion data.

result: The post-natal regression of Peyer's patches in Shpnm/m mice is due to deregulated cell death. Rudimentary Peyer's patches formed in Shpnm/m embryos but regressed post-natally, and combined Casp8 heterozygosity and Ripk3 deletion restored Peyer's patches.
evaluation: Claims C126 and C142 are supported by cited evidence of embryonic Peyer's patch formation and the restoration of Peyer's patches in Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice shown in Figure 9C. This demonstrates that both apoptosis and RIPK3-dependent pathways contribute to Peyer's patch loss.

result: Apoptosis is the main driver of Shpnm/m dermatitis. Sharpin deficiency sensitizes keratinocytes to TNF/TNFR1-induced, caspase-8-mediated apoptosis, and this defect drives the cpdm dermatitis. These findings provide evidence that excessive apoptosis can cause inflammatory disease.
evaluation: Claims C119, C135, C136, and C138 represent the major conclusion of the study and are supported by the combined evidence from genetic deletions (Casp8 heterozygosity delays dermatitis while Mlkl deletion does not), in vitro cell death assays, and caspase cleavage data. This is a well-supported central finding.

result: In the context of the Shpnm/m epidermis, the dominant role of the RIPK1 kinase domain is to activate apoptosis. This interpretation is based on the finding that crossing cpdm mice with Ripk1K45A/K45A mice completely suppresses the phenotype, combined with evidence that Nec-1 blocked TNF-induced caspase-8 and caspase-3 activation in Shpnm/m dermal fibroblasts.
evaluation: Claims C127-C129 and C139 integrate cited work (Berger et al., 2014) with the current findings to propose a novel role for RIPK1 kinase activity in apoptosis. The supporting evidence from Figure 4D showing Nec-1 blocking caspase activation is strong, though this interpretation challenges conventional understanding and may benefit from additional mechanistic studies.

result: TNF/TNFR1 signaling is the main driver of inflammation in cpdm mice and IL-1 contributes to exacerbating the disease, based on head-to-head comparison showing Tnfr1 deletion is more effective than Il1r1 deletion at preventing disease.
evaluation: Claim C116 is supported by the comparative data in Figure 1 showing complete suppression by Tnfr1 deletion versus delayed but not prevented disease with Il1r1 deletion. This establishes the relative importance of these pathways in a controlled comparison.

result: Macrophages may play a role in the amplification of Shpnm/m dermatitis, and myeloid cell death may contribute to the inflammatory skin phenotype, based on early macrophage infiltration and TNF sensitivity of myeloid cells.
evaluation: Claims C63 and C74 are speculative interpretations based on macrophage infiltration (Figure 2B) and myeloid cell TNF sensitivity (Figure 4E). While the observations are sound, the causal role of macrophages and myeloid cell death in disease pathogenesis is not directly tested and remains uncertain.

result: Environmental differences contribute to the variable penetrance of the Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− phenotype, as evidenced by different outcomes at different facilities with different caspase-8 deletion constructs.
evaluation: Claim C134 is supported by the observation of different outcomes at three facilities described in the text and Figure 8. While the specific environmental factors are not identified, the variable penetrance is well-documented and the inference of environmental contribution is reasonable.
